        theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.compact_weight_mem_closure_of_integral_chamber {R : Type u} [Ring R] (k : Type u) [Field k] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] [IsNoetherianRing R] {v : RealProjectiveSpace R} {T : CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty (FGModuleCat R)} (h : T = realStrictTorsion k v ∧ ((∃ (B : FGModuleCat R), T = generatedTorsionClass B) ∨ CovariantlyFinite T) ∨ T = realWeakTorsion k v ∧ ((∃ (N : FGModuleCat R), ∀ (M : FGModuleCat R), T M ↔ Subsingleton (M ⟶ N)) ∨ CovariantlyFinite T)) :
        v ∈ closure {w : RealProjectiveSpace R | ∃ (n : ℕ) (g : ProjectiveClass R), 0 < n ∧ n • w = (realProjectiveClass R) g ∧ ((projectiveClassWeight k) g).strictTorsionClass = T ∧ ((projectiveClassWeight k) g).weakTorsionClass = T ∧ ∀ (M : FGModuleCat R), ((projectiveClassWeight k) g).IsSemistable M → CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero M}

        In every neighborhood of a compact strict or cocompact weak weight one finds a rational weight whose integral multiple has exactly the prescribed torsion class on both sides of the wall test. Covariant finiteness suffices on either side. Its only semistable module is zero.
